title: Accessible Data Table — An ARIA Grid Showcase
description: A showcase table component over a seeded, fictional 200-row nursery inventory: sortable columns with aria-sort, search and category/stock filters, pagination, checkbox row selection with a tri-state select-page box, and a sticky header. It follows the ARIA grid pattern with one tab stop and arrow, Home/End, Ctrl+Home/End and PageUp/PageDown navigation, announces results in a live region, and shows the ARIA attributes of the focused cell in an inspector panel as you move.
prompt: Build 'Accessible Data Table', a showcase data table component with a fictional seeded dataset of about 200 rows. It needs sortable columns with aria-sort, filtering, pagination, row selection with checkboxes, a sticky header, keyboard grid navigation following the ARIA grid pattern (arrows, Home/End, PageUp/PageDown), and a live region announcing sort and filter results. Add a panel that shows the relevant ARIA attributes live for whatever cell has focus. It should look calm and trustworthy, like a well-made design-system component.

methodology: Accessibility-tree oracles instead of pixels: aria-sort on exactly one header, aria-rowcount equal to filtered rows plus the header, aria-rowindex continuing across pages, aria-selected on selected rows.

Keyboard walk against the APG grid pattern: arrows, Home/End, Ctrl+Home/End and PageUp/PageDown are asserted by reading the focused cell's aria-rowindex and aria-colindex, and the grid must keep exactly one tabindex=0 at every step.
Sort correctness is checked against an independent sort of the values read from the rendered cells, numeric and locale-aware text.
Selection state machine: Space, row checkboxes, the tri-state select-page box (indeterminate, checked, cleared on a new page) and a count that persists across pages.
Live-region text is asserted verbatim, since it is the only feedback a screen-reader user gets after sorting or filtering; a manual NVDA pass is still recommended for real announcements.
risks: Losing the single tab stop after a re-render (sorting and paging rebuild the table, so the remembered position is restored and clamped).
Space on a focused checkbox toggling twice (once natively, once by the grid handler).
aria-rowindex restarting at 2 on every page, which would misreport position to screen readers.
The sticky header or wide columns breaking on phones; the table scrolls inside its own box.
qa.playwright: The spec never looks at CSS: focus position comes from document.activeElement's aria-rowindex and aria-colindex, and sort order from data-v attributes on cells, so the tests describe what assistive technology would see. page.keyboard.press covers the modifier combos (Control+Home, Control+End) on both projects. The dataset is generated with a seeded PRNG exposed on window.__table, which lets the filter test compute the expected Fern count rather than hard-code it. The live region is checked with exact text because a wrong announcement is a real accessibility bug.
coverage: aria-sort ascending/descending/single column, numeric and text sort order, live announcement
aria-rowcount after filtering, aria-rowindex on page 2, search, empty state, page size
Full keyboard walk with the single tab stop and header sort via Enter
Space and checkbox selection, tri-state select-page, cross-page count, clear
Inspector updates with focus, seeded dataset reproducibility

a11y: This page is the accessibility exercise: a role=grid table with one roving tab stop, aria-sort, aria-rowcount/rowindex/colindex, aria-selected and labelled checkboxes, keyboard support following the ARIA Authoring Practices grid pattern, and a polite live region for sort, filter, page and selection changes.
